If Nelson could sing, he probably wouldn't have written so many great songs. He wouldn't have reinvented himself 20 years ago into a country music outlaw. He wouldn't constantly organize his friends and famous acquaintances to perform in cultural extravaganzas he originally called ''picnics'' and now titles Farm Aid. If he could sing, he wouldn't be Willie.

Willie Nelson, on his new album Bluegrass pulls 12 songs from his immense catalog, hand picks a group of crack musicians, enlists his long-time producer Buddy Cannon to assist him and then refashions the songs to sound more like the vibrant and resonant Appalachian music that took its name from Bill Monroe and The Bluegrass Boys.

Nelson surely chose these twelve songs to highlight this, but he could have easily selected scores of others from his infinite reserves. That's how deeply rooted his music is in the genre.
